name: Braids
blurb: Woven strands, from single plaits to twin and crown braids
title: Braids Hairstyle Reference: Types, Drawing Tips & Styling
description: Braids reference for illustrators and cosplayers: three-strand, French, fishtail, twin and crown braids, plus how to draw the woven plait pattern.
answer: A braid, or plait, is hair divided into strands that are crossed over each other in a repeating pattern to form one woven rope. The basic version uses three strands; variations change the number of strands, where the weave starts and how many braids are worn.

sections.h: What braids bring to a character
body: Braiding is one of the oldest ways of keeping long hair tidy, and that practical history colours how braids read in design. A single neat plait suggests diligence or a rural, hard-working background; twin braids worn with glasses are a classic shorthand for a studious, quiet student.
A loose side braid over one shoulder softens the face and feels gentle and mature, while a crown braid wrapped over the head borrows from folk costume and feels romantic.

body: Start with a centre line for the braid's path, then draw a tapering tube around it. Fill the tube with alternating segments: each one is a rounded teardrop shape leaning left, then right, tucking under the previous one like a stack of overlapping leaves.
Segments get smaller toward the tie as less hair remains, and the braid should narrow overall. Finish with a band and a short loose tuft so it does not look like a rope cut off.

Where the braid leaves the head, draw the hair being pulled into it: strands converge from the scalp into the first crossing. Braids are stiffer than loose hair, so they swing as a single unit and bend in gentle arcs rather than sharp kinks.

sections.h: Styling braids for cosplay and photos
body: On a wig, braid while the fibres are slightly damp and secure the ends with clear elastics. Pancaking, or gently pulling the outer loops wider, makes a braid look fuller in photos.
Bring braids forward over the shoulders when shooting from the front so they frame the face, or turn the model three-quarters away to show a French or crown braid from behind.

faq.q: What is the difference between a braid and a plait?
faq.a: None in meaning. Plait is more common in British English and braid in American English.

faq.q: How do I draw a braid that looks right?
faq.a: Draw a tapering guide tube first, then fill it with alternating leaf-shaped segments that overlap in one direction.

faq.q: What is the difference between French and Dutch braids?
faq.a: Both add hair as they go. A French braid crosses strands over and lies flat; a Dutch braid crosses them under, so it stands out from the head.
